exposure: mean peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) during sleep
outcome: Free and Cued Selective Reminding Test delayed free recall
cohort: The study included 358 community-dwelling elderly individuals without dementia (mean age 71.0 ± 4.2 years; 42.5% males).
finding: Lower mean peripheral oxygen saturation during sleep and longer time spent with SpO2 <90% were associated with a steeper decline in various cognitive functions, with OSA parameters showing a stronger association in older participants, men, and ApoE4 carriers.
